passages.title: When a Sleep Clinic Comes Closer
passages.source_title: China Focus: Sleepless no more? China scales up sleep care nationwide
passages.source_verification: URL可访问；核验了标题、日期、门诊增长、地级市服务要求及非药物疗法等可见事实。
passages.adaptation_note: 题材参考所列权威来源的公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
passages.content:
For years, a sleep clinic in a county hospital received about 200 visits annually. That number later reached roughly 600. The change does not necessarily mean that three times as many residents suddenly developed insomnia. It may also show that more people recognize sleep problems and are willing to ask for professional help.

Access matters in that decision. Chinese health authorities required every prefecture-level city to have at least one hospital offering sleep-clinic services by the end of 2025. Some places extended the service to county hospitals. When care is nearby, a patient does not have to travel to a famous hospital in a distant city or continue suffering alone.

The wider service also changes what treatment can mean. A sleeping pill is not the only possible response. Clinics may use cognitive behavioral therapy, lifestyle changes, exercise, meditation or medical devices, depending on the patient. Such care is holistic: it considers several connected parts of a person's health rather than one symptom only.

More clinics, therefore, are useful for two reasons. They make help easier to reach, and they can replace a narrow idea of treatment with a fuller examination of why a person cannot sleep well.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why wider sleep-clinic access can improve both help-seeking and treatment
Why all sleep problems have recently tripled
Why large-city hospitals should close their sleep centers
Why medication is the only reliable answer to insomnia
questions.explanation: 全文从就医意愿、服务可及性和多元治疗三方面说明扩大睡眠门诊的意义。
questions.evidence_text: More clinics, therefore, are useful for two reasons. They make help easier to reach, and they can replace a narrow idea of treatment with a fuller examination of why a person cannot sleep well.

questions.question: What were prefecture-level cities required to provide by the end of 2025?
options: A free meditation class in every neighborhood
At least one hospital with sleep-clinic services
A famous specialist in every county
Three times as many hospital beds
questions.explanation: 第二段直接说明每个地级市至少要有一家医院提供睡眠门诊服务。
questions.evidence_text: Chinese health authorities required every prefecture-level city to have at least one hospital offering sleep-clinic services by the end of 2025.

questions.question: What does “holistic” most nearly mean in the passage?
options: Limited to one medicine
Designed only for young people
Considering connected parts of health
Available only in major cities
questions.explanation: 冒号后的解释表明 holistic 指综合考虑健康中彼此关联的多个部分。
questions.evidence_text: Such care is holistic: it considers several connected parts of a person's health rather than one symptom only.

questions.question: Why might clinic visits rise even without an equal rise in insomnia?
options: Patients may be more willing and able to seek help.
Hospitals may count every visitor three times.
Exercise may cause sleep disorders.
County clinics may refuse local residents.
questions.explanation: 文章指出增长也可能反映认知提高、求助意愿增强及服务距离缩短，而非患病人数同比增长。
questions.evidence_text: It may also show that more people recognize sleep problems and are willing to ask for professional help.

questions.question: How does the author view the expansion of sleep clinics?
options: Supportive because it improves access and broadens care
Doubtful because nearby care has no practical value
Alarmed because all non-drug treatments are unsafe
Indifferent because treatment choices never change
questions.explanation: 结尾明确肯定更多门诊在可及性与治疗观念上的双重价值。
questions.evidence_text: They make help easier to reach, and they can replace a narrow idea of treatment with a fuller examination of why a person cannot sleep well.

passages.title: A Healthy Plate Begins Before Dinner
passages.source_title: Guideline aims to promote balanced nutrition, healthier lifestyles
passages.source_verification: URL可访问；核验了标题、日期、2030目标、盐糖油与膳食纤维建议，以及全供应链思路。
passages.adaptation_note: 题材参考所列权威来源的公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
passages.content:
Advice about healthy eating often arrives at the dinner table: use less salt, choose fresh fruit, or carefully control the size of a meal. A national food and nutrition guideline for 2025-2030 takes a wider view. It treats the meal as the final point in a much longer system.

The guideline gives consumers clear reference points. It aims to raise daily fiber intake to 25-30 grams, limit salt to 5 grams, and keep added sugar at 25 grams. Yet information alone cannot guarantee a better diet. A family may understand the numbers but still find nutritious food expensive, unavailable or difficult to prepare.

For that reason, the plan begins before food reaches a kitchen. It connects nutrition with breeding, farming, processing, storage, transport and cooking. Research can improve the quality of products, while smarter storage may reduce waste. Portion-control tools can also turn an abstract recommendation into an action a cook can repeat. In this sense, abstract means existing mainly as an idea rather than as an immediately usable step.

This approach does not remove personal responsibility. People still decide what to buy and eat. However, it recognizes that choice is shaped by supply and price. A healthy plate is more likely when public information and the food system point in the same direction.

questions.question: What central idea does the passage develop?
options: Healthy eating depends on both personal choices and the food system
Nutrition targets should be kept secret from consumers
Food waste matters more than human health
Families should grow every food they eat
questions.explanation: 文章由餐桌建议转向供应链，最后强调个人选择与食物系统需要同向作用。
questions.evidence_text: A healthy plate is more likely when public information and the food system point in the same direction.

questions.question: What daily salt limit is mentioned?
options: 5 grams
25 grams
30 grams
50 grams
questions.explanation: 第二段明确给出每日盐摄入限制为5克。
questions.evidence_text: It aims to raise daily fiber intake to 25-30 grams, limit salt to 5 grams, and keep added sugar at 25 grams.

questions.question: What does “abstract” mean here?
options: Too costly to measure
Mainly an idea, not yet a usable step
Produced on a farm
Easy to repeat every day
questions.explanation: 正文在该词后直接给出语境定义。
questions.evidence_text: In this sense, abstract means existing mainly as an idea rather than as an immediately usable step.

questions.question: Why does the plan include storage and transport?
options: Because diet is affected by how nutritious food reaches people
Because consumers are unable to learn simple numbers
Because cooking should be removed from homes
Because every product must have the same price
questions.explanation: 文章指出选择受供应和价格影响，因此储运等环节会影响健康食物是否可得。
questions.evidence_text: However, it recognizes that choice is shaped by supply and price.

questions.question: What is the author's attitude toward personal responsibility?
options: It remains important but is not the whole explanation.
It should be replaced entirely by government action.
It has no connection with daily meals.
It matters only to food researchers.
questions.explanation: 作者既保留个人选择责任，又指出系统条件会塑造选择，态度是有保留的肯定。
questions.evidence_text: This approach does not remove personal responsibility. People still decide what to buy and eat.

passages.title: What a Fitness Survey Can—and Cannot—Do
passages.source_verification: URL可访问；核验了抽样规模、年龄范围、实时上传、新指标、历次监测与个性化建议。
passages.adaptation_note: 题材参考所列权威来源的公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
passages.content:
A national fitness survey can look like a giant collection of pushups, body measurements and detailed questionnaires. China's sixth monitoring campaign, conducted across 31 provincial-level regions, planned to gather information from 248,000 people aged 3 to 79. But the real value of such a survey lies less in any single score than in the comparisons it makes possible.

Repeated every five years, the campaign can reveal movement that an individual may not notice. The 2020 report, for example, found modest overall progress while also recording rising weight and weaker muscular strength in some groups. The latest campaign added measures related to particular exercises and required weight and body mass index. Data were uploaded to a national platform in real time for the first time, a step intended to improve authenticity. Here, authenticity refers to confidence that records reflect what was actually measured.

National patterns can guide decisions about public fitness facilities or programs. Local results can serve another purpose. At one testing site, experts offered exercise suggestions based on each person's weaknesses; one participant discovered a balance problem and planned targeted training. Thus, the same measurement may inform both a policy and a private routine.

Still, a survey is a map, not the journey. It can identify a weak area, but it cannot exercise on someone's behalf. Nor does an average describe every citizen. Good monitoring therefore requires two careful moves: compare groups without hiding their differences, and connect diagnosis with realistic opportunities to act.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly concerned with?
options: The uses and limits of large-scale fitness monitoring
The rules of a national pushup competition
The replacement of exercise by data collection
The history of one local sports center
questions.explanation: 文章说明监测如何服务公共政策与个人训练，同时强调数据不能替代行动且平均数不能代表所有人。
questions.evidence_text: Still, a survey is a map, not the journey.

questions.question: What was new about the handling of data in the latest campaign?
options: It was uploaded in real time to a national platform.
It was collected only from senior citizens.
It excluded body weight and exercise habits.
It was kept separately by every participant.
questions.explanation: 第二段直接说明首次实时上传至国家平台。
questions.evidence_text: Data were uploaded to a national platform in real time for the first time, a step intended to improve authenticity.

questions.question: What does “authenticity” refer to in this passage?
options: The popularity of a sport
Confidence that measurements are genuine
The difficulty of a questionnaire
Agreement between every age group
questions.explanation: 同句后半部分给出了该词的明确定义。
questions.evidence_text: Here, authenticity refers to confidence that records reflect what was actually measured.

questions.question: Why does the author mention the participant with a balance problem?
options: To show how broad data can lead to an individual action
To prove that balance is the only important fitness measure
To argue that national averages are always wrong
To suggest that experts should avoid personal advice
questions.explanation: 该例承接“地方结果的另一用途”，展示测量如何转化为个人针对性训练。
questions.evidence_text: At one testing site, experts offered exercise suggestions based on each person's weaknesses; one participant discovered a balance problem and planned targeted training.

questions.question: How does the author assess fitness monitoring?
options: Useful when interpreted carefully and linked to action
Worthless unless every citizen receives one score
Sufficient by itself to improve public health
Dangerous because comparisons are never fair
questions.explanation: 作者肯定监测的诊断作用，同时用两个条件限定其价值。
questions.evidence_text: Good monitoring therefore requires two careful moves: compare groups without hiding their differences, and connect diagnosis with realistic opportunities to act.

passages.title: The Work Hidden Inside One Life-Expectancy Target
passages.source_title: China targets average life expectancy of 80 by 2030 in new five-year health plan
passages.source_verification: URL可访问；核验了80岁目标、2025基线、控烟、全生命周期服务、基层资源、康复人才与病历共享。
passages.adaptation_note: 题材参考所列权威来源的公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
passages.content:
A target of 80 years is easy to repeat. It is also easy to misunderstand. China's health plan for 2026-2030 aims to raise average life expectancy from 79.25 years in 2025 to 80 by 2030. The difference appears small, yet a national average changes only when many risks are reduced across a very large population. The headline number is therefore better read as a summary of coordinated work than as a promise about any one person's lifespan.

Some measures try to prevent illness before hospital treatment is needed. The plan seeks smoke-free environments and stronger cessation services, with a target of reducing smoking among people aged 15 and above to 20 percent. Other measures follow people through different stages of life: cancer screening and HPV vaccination for eligible girls, occupational-health protection, and better care for older adults with disabilities or dementia. This life-cycle approach recognizes that the most relevant risk is not identical at age 13, 40 and 80.

Access creates a second challenge. Major hospitals may offer advanced treatment, but routine prevention and rehabilitation must also be available near where people live. The plan therefore calls for locally appropriate primary-care distribution and more rehabilitation professionals. It also proposes cross-provincial sharing of records and medical images. Interoperable records—records that different systems can exchange and use—could spare patients repeated tests, although technology cannot compensate for an absent clinic or an overworked therapist.

The life-expectancy target has political force because it is measurable. Its weakness is that an average can rise while some regions or groups remain behind. Success should therefore be judged twice: first by the national figure, and then by whether preventive care, skilled workers and usable services become more evenly available.

questions.question: What argument does the passage make about the 80-year target?
options: It summarizes many connected health efforts and must be checked against fair access.
It guarantees that every citizen will live to exactly 80.
It can be achieved mainly by expanding major hospitals.
It makes prevention and rehabilitation unnecessary.
questions.explanation: 文章把单一指标拆解为预防、全生命周期服务、基层可及性与公平性，并要求双重评价。
questions.evidence_text: The headline number is therefore better read as a summary of coordinated work than as a promise about any one person's lifespan.

questions.question: Which smoking-related goal does the plan include?
options: Reducing the rate among people aged 15 and above to 20 percent
Ending all tobacco sales before 2027
Providing cessation services only in major hospitals
Measuring smoking only among older adults
questions.explanation: 第二段明确给出15岁及以上人群吸烟率降至20%的目标。
questions.evidence_text: The plan seeks smoke-free environments and stronger cessation services, with a target of reducing smoking among people aged 15 and above to 20 percent.

questions.question: What are “interoperable” records?
options: Records that different systems can exchange and use
Records available only to one local clinic
Paper records that cannot be copied
Records containing no medical images
questions.explanation: 破折号之间直接定义了 interoperable。
questions.evidence_text: Interoperable records—records that different systems can exchange and use—could spare patients repeated tests, although technology cannot compensate for an absent clinic or an overworked therapist.

questions.question: Why does the author say the 0.75-year rise only appears small?
options: Moving a national average requires improvements affecting many people and risks.
The 2025 figure was calculated for only one hospital.
Life expectancy is unrelated to public services.
The plan actually intends a much lower figure.
questions.explanation: 前后句构成隐含对比：数字差距小，但改变全国平均值需要大规模、多风险协同行动。
questions.evidence_text: The difference appears small, yet a national average changes only when many risks are reduced across a very large population.

questions.question: What is the author's view of a national average as a success measure?
options: Valuable but incomplete without distributional evidence
Meaningless under all circumstances
More important than every health service
Useful only for comparing individuals
questions.explanation: 结尾认可指标的可测量性，同时警示平均值会遮蔽落后地区或群体。
questions.evidence_text: Its weakness is that an average can rise while some regions or groups remain behind.

passages.title: Why Prevention Must Become an Operating Principle
passages.source_title: China to promote national health during 14th Five-Year Plan
passages.source_verification: URL可访问；核验了预防优先、资源差距、应急体系、心理健康、重点群体及服务创新等可见事实。
passages.adaptation_note: 题材参考所列权威来源的公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
passages.content:
Health policy is often judged at the hospital door: Was treatment available, quick and affordable? A 2022 national plan for the 2021-2025 period proposed a wider test. It placed prevention, emergency readiness, everyday living conditions and equitable basic services inside the same health framework. The important shift was conceptual. Health was not to be treated merely as the medical sector's product, but as a consideration running through public policy.

That principle matters because many causes of illness arise before a patient enters a clinic. Food and drug safety, working conditions, mental-health support, infection control and the physical environment shape who becomes ill and when. Monitoring and early-warning systems can also detect a threat before ordinary treatment capacity is overwhelmed. Prevention in this sense is anticipatory: it acts in view of a risk rather than waiting for damage to become fully visible.

Yet broad responsibility can produce a familiar administrative problem. If health belongs to every policy, each institution may assume that another one will handle it. A slogan becomes operational only when duties, indicators and channels for coordination are specified. The plan's attention to emergency mechanisms, chronic-disease management and services for women, children, older people, workers and people with disabilities illustrates the range involved; it does not by itself prove that gaps have closed.

Equity complicates evaluation further. An increase in national life expectancy may coexist with unequal access between urban and rural communities or among regions and social groups. Faster registration and day-care services improve efficiency for those who reach a facility, whereas a shortage of primary care leaves a different barrier untouched. These are related achievements, not interchangeable ones.

A prevention-first system should consequently be assessed through a chain of evidence: whether risks were identified, whether responsible bodies acted, whether basic services became reachable, and whether disadvantaged groups experienced improvement. The strongest promise of the plan is not a single target. It is the claim that health outcomes should be traced back to the institutions and conditions that produce them.

questions.question: What is the passage's central claim?
options: Prevention becomes meaningful when health responsibility is translated into coordinated, equitable action.
Hospital speed is the only valid measure of a health system.
National averages make local evidence unnecessary.
Every public institution already performs identical health duties.
questions.explanation: 全文论证预防优先必须从概念转化为明确责任、协作、服务可及性与公平证据。
questions.evidence_text: A slogan becomes operational only when duties, indicators and channels for coordination are specified.

questions.question: Which factor does the passage identify as shaping health before clinical treatment?
options: Working conditions
Hospital decoration
Medical school rankings
The number of newspaper reports
questions.explanation: 第二段列出工作条件等在就医前就影响健康的因素。
questions.evidence_text: Food and drug safety, working conditions, mental-health support, infection control and the physical environment shape who becomes ill and when.

questions.question: What does “anticipatory” mean in the passage?
options: Responding only after treatment fails
Acting with a future risk in mind
Limited to hospital registration
Unrelated to visible damage
questions.explanation: 冒号后的释义说明它指在风险完全造成损害前采取行动。
questions.evidence_text: Prevention in this sense is anticipatory: it acts in view of a risk rather than waiting for damage to become fully visible.

questions.question: Why might declaring health to be part of every policy be insufficient?
options: Shared responsibility can become unclear responsibility without assigned duties.
Public policy cannot affect health conditions.
Only doctors are permitted to collect evidence.
Prevention always costs more than emergency treatment.
questions.explanation: 作者指出广泛责任可能导致机构互相等待，因此需要明确职责和协调渠道。
questions.evidence_text: If health belongs to every policy, each institution may assume that another one will handle it.

questions.question: What does the contrast between faster registration and scarce primary care show?
options: Efficiency at a facility does not automatically solve geographic or service access.
Registration should be removed from all hospitals.
Primary care and day care are the same achievement.
Rural communities do not need medical facilities.
questions.explanation: 该对比区分了到院后的效率与能否获得基层服务这两个不可互换的维度。
questions.evidence_text: Faster registration and day-care services improve efficiency for those who reach a facility, whereas a shortage of primary care leaves a different barrier untouched.

passages.title: Training the Teacher Who Understands Both Sides
passages.source_title: China's first bachelor's program in AI education to address teacher shortage
passages.source_verification: URL可访问；核验了项目定位、技术与教育双模块、伦理和数据安全课程及协作实践模式。
passages.adaptation_note: 题材参考所列权威来源的公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
passages.content:
A school can buy an AI tool in a day, but preparing a teacher to use it well takes much longer. Beijing Normal University launched an undergraduate program in AI education because schools need people who understand both the technology and the classroom.

The course design joins two kinds of knowledge. Students study machine learning, natural language processing and educational data. They also learn psychology, learning theory, lesson design and assessment. This combination matters because a technically impressive tool may still be unsuitable for a child's age or a lesson's purpose. Meanwhile, a skilled classroom teacher cannot examine an AI system's limits without some technical understanding.

The program includes AI ethics and data security as required subjects. It also plans practical courses and cooperation among the university, companies and schools. Such cooperation is interdisciplinary: it brings knowledge from different fields together around one problem. Students can therefore test ideas in real teaching settings instead of treating education as a simple market for new software.

Graduates may become AI teachers, develop learning platforms, conduct research or help shape policy. These paths differ, but they share one principle: technology should serve education. The program's real answer to the teacher shortage is not merely to produce more AI specialists. It is to prepare specialists who can ask what learning needs before deciding what a machine should do.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the new program?
options: To train people who combine AI knowledge with educational judgment
To replace all classroom teachers with software
To teach machine learning without any school practice
To limit graduates to one kind of job
questions.explanation: 全文强调技术知识与教育判断的结合，而不只是增加纯技术人才。
questions.evidence_text: The program's real answer to the teacher shortage is not merely to produce more AI specialists.

questions.question: Which subjects are required in the program?
options: AI ethics and data security
Painting and music history
Hospital management and nutrition
Only programming contests
questions.explanation: 第三段直接说明人工智能伦理和数据安全是必修内容。
questions.evidence_text: The program includes AI ethics and data security as required subjects.

questions.question: What does “interdisciplinary” mean here?
options: Keeping companies away from schools
Using only one academic subject
Bringing different fields together
Studying without practical experience
questions.explanation: 冒号后的内容直接解释该词含义。
questions.evidence_text: Such cooperation is interdisciplinary: it brings knowledge from different fields together around one problem.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention a tool that is unsuitable for a child's age?
options: To show that technical quality alone does not ensure educational value
To prove that young people cannot use any technology
To argue that lesson purposes never matter
To suggest that teachers need no AI knowledge
questions.explanation: 该例说明技术上出色并不等于教育上合适，因此教师需要双重知识。
questions.evidence_text: This combination matters because a technically impressive tool may still be unsuitable for a child's age or a lesson's purpose.

questions.question: How does the author view technology's role in education?
options: It should be guided by learning needs.
It should determine every lesson goal.
It has value only in private companies.
It makes teacher preparation unnecessary.
questions.explanation: 结尾把学习需要置于机器功能之前，表明技术应服务教育目标。
questions.evidence_text: It is to prepare specialists who can ask what learning needs before deciding what a machine should do.

passages.title: An AI School as a Campus Experiment
passages.source_title: Tsinghua University to launch new school for AI talent development
passages.source_verification: 清单URL本轮直接打开失败；经同标题检索核验到新华社可见页面（不同内容ID），确认标题、日期、约150人计划及117门试点课程、147个课堂等事实。
passages.adaptation_note: 题材参考所列权威来源的公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
passages.content:
When a university opens a school devoted to artificial intelligence, the obvious question is how many AI experts it will produce. Tsinghua University's plan offers another question: can AI also change the way those experts are educated?

The new undergraduate school planned to enroll about 150 students in its first year. Its goal was not limited to technical training. It would combine AI with several disciplines and develop students' literacy, expertise and capacity for innovation. That design reflects a basic fact: many important uses of AI occur in medicine, engineering, science or the humanities rather than inside a single computer laboratory.

The wider university had already started testing AI in teaching. It reported 117 pilot courses and 147 classes using AI-supported methods, along with teaching assistants, lesson-planning aids and automated grading systems. These trials make the campus a kind of laboratory for the new school. Faculty members can observe where a tool saves time, where it confuses students, and where human review remains necessary. A pilot is a limited test conducted before a larger decision.

The numbers, however, should not be mistaken for proof of better learning. Counting tools or classes is easier than measuring whether students ask deeper questions or transfer knowledge across fields. The school will be most valuable if it studies its own educational experiments as carefully as it studies AI itself.

questions.question: What main question does the passage raise about the new school?
options: Whether it can improve both AI talent training and educational practice
Whether it can eliminate every nontechnical subject
Whether 150 students can build a computer laboratory
Whether automated grading should become the only assessment
questions.explanation: 文章不只关注培养多少专家，还关注人工智能如何改变培养方式及其效果评价。
questions.evidence_text: Tsinghua University's plan offers another question: can AI also change the way those experts are educated?

questions.question: About how many students did the school plan to enroll in its first year?
questions.explanation: 第二段首句明确给出约150人的首年招生计划。
questions.evidence_text: The new undergraduate school planned to enroll about 150 students in its first year.

questions.question: What is a “pilot” in the passage?
options: A person who flies an aircraft
A final national examination
A limited test before a larger decision
A course without any teacher
questions.explanation: 正文紧接该词给出定义。
questions.evidence_text: A pilot is a limited test conducted before a larger decision.

questions.question: Why does the author call the campus a laboratory?
options: Existing classroom trials can provide evidence for improving the new model.
All university buildings are being replaced by laboratories.
Students will study only chemistry and medicine.
AI tools have already proved that human review is unnecessary.
questions.explanation: “实验室”是比喻，指已有试点能让教师观察工具的效果、问题和人工审核需求。
questions.evidence_text: Faculty members can observe where a tool saves time, where it confuses students, and where human review remains necessary.

questions.question: How does the author treat the reported numbers of AI-supported classes?
options: As useful activity measures, but not proof of learning quality
As final proof that every student learns better
As evidence that no further study is needed
As irrelevant because tools cannot support teachers
questions.explanation: 最后一段明确区分活动数量与学习质量证据。
questions.evidence_text: The numbers, however, should not be mistaken for proof of better learning.

passages.title: Opening an AI Academy Without Closing the Door
passages.source_title: Across China: Teen AI academies pave way for China's next-gen innovators
passages.source_verification: URL直接打开偶发内部错误；同URL搜索结果可见全文，核验了北京与上海项目、31所高校资源、科研参与及海淀项目招生数据。
passages.adaptation_note: 题材参考所列权威来源的公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
passages.content:
Teen AI academies in Beijing and Shanghai are designed as bridges. They connect secondary schools with universities, research projects and industry practice. In Beijing, one academy planned to draw on faculty from 31 universities and let students participate in national-level research. A related Haidian program teaches computational thinking, mathematics, programming and AI fundamentals on weekends and holidays.

Such programs can offer an experience that an ordinary timetable rarely provides. A teenager may encounter an unsolved problem, work with a researcher and see how mathematics becomes a model. Early depth can be valuable, especially in a field advancing too quickly for textbooks alone.

The bridge, however, has an entrance. In 2024, the Haidian experimental class accepted 180 students after receiving more than 1,500 applications; the reported admission rate was 11.76 percent. Selectivity may help a demanding course operate, but it also raises a design question. If the public purpose is to build a broad talent pipeline, what should happen to interested students who are not selected? A pipeline is a continuing route through which learners can develop, not merely a contest that identifies a few winners.

One answer is a layered system. Intensive academies can provide research opportunities to a smaller group, while regular schools offer basic AI literacy, open projects and routes to later entry. Selection should also look for curiosity and persistence, not only prior programming experience, because earlier access to devices and tutoring is uneven.

The success of a teen academy should therefore be measured in two directions. It should help advanced learners move farther, but its methods and resources should also strengthen the wider educational path from which future applicants emerge.

questions.question: What problem does the passage examine?
options: How selective AI academies can support excellence without weakening broad access
Why teenagers should avoid university research
How weekend classes can replace regular schools
Why every applicant must enter the same intensive course
questions.explanation: 文章既认可高强度项目，又追问未入选者的成长路径，中心是卓越培养与广泛机会的平衡。
questions.evidence_text: The bridge, however, has an entrance.

questions.question: What opportunities did the Beijing academy plan to offer?
options: Faculty resources from 31 universities and participation in research
Guaranteed admission for more than 1,500 applicants
Only recorded lessons with no projects
A curriculum limited to textbook reading
questions.explanation: 第一段直接说明31所高校师资与国家级科研参与机会。
questions.evidence_text: In Beijing, one academy planned to draw on faculty from 31 universities and let students participate in national-level research.

questions.question: What does “pipeline” mean in the passage?
options: A machine used in an AI laboratory
A continuing route for learner development
A single entrance examination
A list of university buildings
questions.explanation: 正文明确把 pipeline 解释为学习者持续发展的路径。
questions.evidence_text: A pipeline is a continuing route through which learners can develop, not merely a contest that identifies a few winners.

questions.question: Why might prior programming experience be an unfair main selection standard?
options: Access to devices and tutoring differs among students.
Programming has no connection with AI.
Curiosity can be measured perfectly by one test.
All applicants have already joined research projects.
questions.explanation: 文章指出先前资源获取不均，因此以既有编程经验为主会把机会差异误作能力差异。
questions.evidence_text: Selection should also look for curiosity and persistence, not only prior programming experience, because earlier access to devices and tutoring is uneven.

questions.question: What is the author's view of intensive teen AI academies?
options: Positive, provided they contribute to a broader learning system
Opposed, because advanced learning is always harmful
Uncritical, because selectivity needs no explanation
Indifferent, because their resources cannot be shared
questions.explanation: 作者认可其深度价值，但把资源外溢和更广路径作为成功条件。
questions.evidence_text: It should help advanced learners move farther, but its methods and resources should also strengthen the wider educational path from which future applicants emerge.

passages.title: The Smart Playground Still Needs a Teacher
passages.source_title: Chinese schools start new semester with more AI-empowered facilities
passages.source_verification: URL可访问；核验了智能体育场、可穿戴心率数据、英语口语反馈、184个试点基地及大班教学背景。
passages.adaptation_note: 题材参考所列权威来源的公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
passages.content:
On a smart playground, a three-minute rope-skipping test can produce an immediate score and ranking. In another class, a wrist device reports heart rate while students exercise. Elsewhere, a small terminal comments on a learner's English pronunciation and grammar. These systems promise something teachers in large classes have always lacked: a quick view of each student's performance.

Speed, however, changes the teacher's problem rather than solving it. A heart-rate alert may signal that an exercise should be adjusted, but it does not know whether a child is ill, frightened or simply unfamiliar with the task. A pronunciation score can locate a repeated sound error, yet the teacher must decide whether correction, encouragement or more listening will help. Data become educational only after someone interprets them in context.

The scale of new facilities makes that judgment especially important. One smart playground described in the source covered 16,000 square meters and was intended to serve more than 7,000 students and 700 teachers. Nationally, 184 primary and secondary schools had been named AI education pilot bases in early 2024. A pilot base is expected to explore methods, not merely display equipment.

There are also questions that convenience can hide. Facial recognition may reduce the time needed to record performance, while creating duties concerning consent, storage and access. Instant rankings may motivate some students but embarrass others. Personalized assistance can narrow a learning gap only if devices work reliably and teachers have time to respond. Otherwise, the system produces finer descriptions of unequal outcomes without changing them.

The useful contrast is not between technology and teachers. It is between automatic measurement and informed action. Smart facilities earn their place when they give teachers better evidence, protect students and lead to decisions that a score cannot make by itself.

questions.question: What is the passage's main argument?
options: Smart school data have value only when teachers interpret and act on them responsibly.
Automatic rankings should replace teacher assessment.
Large classes make personalized help impossible under all conditions.
Schools should use AI only in physical education.
questions.explanation: 全文以多种设备为例，区分自动测量与教师基于情境的判断和行动。
questions.evidence_text: Data become educational only after someone interprets them in context.

questions.question: How large was the smart playground mentioned?
options: 1,600 square meters
7,000 square meters
16,000 square meters
184 square meters
questions.explanation: 第三段明确给出16,000平方米。
questions.evidence_text: One smart playground described in the source covered 16,000 square meters and was intended to serve more than 7,000 students and 700 teachers.

questions.question: What is a “pilot base” expected to do?
options: Test and develop methods
Display equipment only
Store every student's private data forever
Remove teachers from decision-making
questions.explanation: 正文用“explore methods”界定试点基地的职责。
questions.evidence_text: A pilot base is expected to explore methods, not merely display equipment.

questions.question: Why does the author compare a heart-rate alert with a child's condition?
options: To show that the same number can require different responses in context
To show that wrist devices always report false information
To prove that children should not exercise at school
To argue that teachers can diagnose every illness
questions.explanation: 数据只能提示异常，疾病、恐惧或不熟悉任务等不同情境需要教师作不同判断。
questions.evidence_text: A heart-rate alert may signal that an exercise should be adjusted, but it does not know whether a child is ill, frightened or simply unfamiliar with the task.

questions.question: How does the author view facial recognition in school sports?
options: As efficient but accompanied by privacy responsibilities
As harmless because it saves teachers time
As useless for recording performance
As acceptable only when rankings are public
questions.explanation: 作者同时指出记录效率和同意、存储、访问方面的责任，态度审慎。
questions.evidence_text: Facial recognition may reduce the time needed to record performance, while creating duties concerning consent, storage and access.

passages.title: AI Literacy Is More Than Learning to Prompt
passages.source_title: Yearender-China Focus: AI takes root in basic education, nurturing future innovators
passages.source_verification: URL直接打开偶发内部错误；同URL搜索结果可见全文，核验了天津分层课程、北京课时、教师培训、人机边界、作业禁令与伦理风险。
passages.adaptation_note: 题材参考所列权威来源的公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
passages.content:
Basic AI education teaches students to obtain a polished answer. A harder version asks when that answer deserves trust, what was lost in producing it, and whether using it serves the learning goal. China's school programs increasingly describe their aim as AI literacy rather than technical specialization, a distinction with consequences for curriculum, assessment and teacher preparation.

A tiered curriculum illustrates the idea. In Tianjin, fourth- and eighth-grade students were assigned one compulsory AI class each week, while other grades could use school-designed courses or integrate AI into existing subjects. Beijing required a minimum of eight AI classes per academic year, moving from experience in primary school toward application and then project work. Progression here is developmental rather than merely cumulative: older learners are expected to make more independent judgments, not simply collect more commands.

That judgment is difficult to assess. A successful program might enable a student to model a physical process, question biased output, protect personal data and explain why a tool should be refused for a particular task. None of these achievements is captured well by counting logins. Nor can schools assume that installing software creates capacity. Teachers across subjects need training, usable lesson materials and time to redesign activities; families also need enough understanding to recognize unhealthy dependence.

Boundaries make the educational purpose visible. National guidance reported in 2025 prohibited submitting AI-generated material directly as homework or exam answers and called for safeguards in creative assignments. The restriction is not anti-technology. It protects the intellectual work that an assignment is meant to reveal. Human-AI collaboration is valuable only if the human remains cognitively present—forming questions, checking claims and taking responsibility for the result.

There is nevertheless a policy tension. Broad access can reduce gaps in exposure, yet uneven devices, connectivity and teacher confidence may turn a common curriculum into unequal experiences. Moreover, privacy protection, algorithmic bias and data security are not optional advanced topics; they determine whether routine participation is safe. AI literacy should therefore be evaluated as a public capability: the capacity to use, question and sometimes decline an automated system. Teaching students to prompt is one component. Teaching them to remain authors of their decisions is the larger task.

questions.question: How does the passage define meaningful AI literacy?
options: As the capacity to use, question and sometimes reject AI while retaining responsibility
As the ability to obtain polished answers as quickly as possible
As early specialization in software engineering for every child
As the number of AI systems installed by a school
questions.explanation: 全文把AI素养界定为使用、质疑、拒绝和承担责任的综合公共能力。
questions.evidence_text: AI literacy should therefore be evaluated as a public capability: the capacity to use, question and sometimes decline an automated system.

questions.question: What did the reported national guidance prohibit?
options: Using simulations in physics lessons
Submitting AI-generated material directly as homework or exam answers
Teaching data security in primary schools
Providing teachers with digital lesson materials
questions.explanation: 第四段直接说明不得将AI生成内容直接作为作业或考试答案提交。
questions.evidence_text: National guidance reported in 2025 prohibited submitting AI-generated material directly as homework or exam answers and called for safeguards in creative assignments.

questions.question: What does “developmental rather than merely cumulative” imply?
options: Students should exercise greater judgment as they mature, not just learn more commands.
Older students should repeat the same introductory lesson.
Course quality can be measured by total logins.
Technical commands should replace project work.
questions.explanation: 冒号后直接说明年级递进强调独立判断，而不是命令数量累加。
questions.evidence_text: Progression here is developmental rather than merely cumulative: older learners are expected to make more independent judgments, not simply collect more commands.

questions.question: Why does the author say the homework restriction is not anti-technology?
options: Because it preserves the thinking that the assignment is designed to assess
Because AI-generated answers are always factually correct
Because schools intend to ban all creative assignments
Because human review makes privacy irrelevant
questions.explanation: 禁令针对替代学习过程的用法，而非技术本身，目的是保留作业所要呈现的思考。
questions.evidence_text: It protects the intellectual work that an assignment is meant to reveal.

questions.question: How could a common AI curriculum still produce unequal experiences?
options: Schools differ in devices, connectivity and teacher readiness.
Every student receives identical support at home.
AI literacy excludes questions of access.
Counting logins removes all resource gaps.
questions.explanation: 共同课程不等于实施条件相同，设备、网络和教师信心差异会改变学生的真实体验。
questions.evidence_text: Broad access can reduce gaps in exposure, yet uneven devices, connectivity and teacher confidence may turn a common curriculum into unequal experiences.
